DesignGroutMix.gml:name: MIX-A — Very Severe (Mg<1000) Design Mix

Remark.content: Per 70-TMSS-03 Rev.02 Table 8B, appended in full to GSL-31136-Geotech-Final-Report.pdf (and its own extracted copy, GSL-31136-Geotech-Report-MA .xlsx) - documents not available when this design was first authored. CORRECTED from an earlier version that used the Table 8B row for Mg>1000 ppm (Type I cement, Fly Ash admixture, max W/BM=0.36): GSL-31136 5.4.3's own chemical analysis (BS 1377 Part 3) measured magnesium at 571-954 ppm across all three tested boreholes/depths - every value below 1000 ppm - while sulphate (5810-8515 ppm) and chloride (0.510-0.705%) both clear the >2000 ppm / >0.10% thresholds, and the site is stated as Very Severe exposure. That combination selects a DIFFERENT row of the same table: Type I (C3A 8-14%) cement with Silica Fume admixture, max W/BM=0.40, min binding material 390 kg/m3 (cement+SCM), max Cl in concrete 0.10%, min f'c 38 MPa (Note 1) - not the Fly Ash/0.36 row this design used before.

Table 8B fixes only the cement type, admixture type, the maximum W/BM ratio and the minimum binder content - it states no batch recipe, and neither FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 nor GSL-31136-Geotech-Final-Report (nor their extracted CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx / GSL-31136-Geotech-Report-MA .xlsx workbooks) states one either. The proportions below are therefore an INFERRED, illustrative design meeting the stated constraints, not a project-specified recipe: an 8% silica fume replacement of total binder by mass (within ACI 234R's typical 5-10% dosage range for durability applications - a literature value, not project-stated); the maximum W/BM (0.40) used directly as the design value, matching how the earlier Fly Ash version used its own ceiling (0.36); an assumed 2% air content; and specific gravities cement=3.15 (Table 8B), silica fume=2.2 (typical/literature, not project-stated), sand=2.65, water=1.0. Mix proportions expressed per 1 m3 of concrete.

Three compressive strength figures appear in the project record, for different purposes. 25 MPa is the structural design value (FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Table 4 and its extracted copy, CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx) - also the fck used in modulusDesign below. 30 MPa is the owner's minimum for construction, set in ASEC's review of submittal DTS-114 R03 (ref. 40611302/46438-J/24, 13/11/2024, comment 7: construction 30 MPa, design 25 MPa; the contractor accepted it); it is the acceptance threshold in crit-grout-strength-qc-min and crit-grout-strength-qc-mean, applied to all 41 batches because nothing in the record shows the grout design changed after the letter. 70-TMSS-03 Table 8B Note 1 separately sets f'c >= 38 MPa for Very Severe/Severe exposure - a durability, not a structural, minimum. strengthDesign here keeps the higher, governing 38 MPa value; all three are satisfied in practice, with margin.

modulusDesign is newly populated (previously absent - the element exists for exactly this purpose, per its own schema documentation, but had never been instantiated on this object). EY = 3700 x fck^(1/3), per ASIRI 2012 Clause 3.1.1.4 as cited in FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Section 6, fck = 25 MPa (the report's own "not less than" design value) -> EY = 10,818,866 kPa (~10.82 GPa). This is the CMC column stiffness the settlement calculation (FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Sections 6/8) uses, distinct from strengthDesign.

One mix design covers the whole program, confirmed on this pass, not one per zone: FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Section 8 states a single method and a single set of governing standards applied uniformly across all nine zones (matching the single-basis finding already recorded on RIProgramBasis[ripb-01]); the Load Transfer Platform is a separate, non-cementitious compacted granular fill (DesignRILTP), not a second grout/concrete mix. No additional DesignGroutMix is warranted. CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx also carries real per-batch field data (41 batches, 1,099 CMCs, cast 14-Oct-2024 to 16-Dec-2024, 7-day and 28-day cylinder strengths, all 41 batches passing the 25 MPa threshold, 28-day range 40.7-54.5 MPa/average 46.6 MPa) that the still-open "realized grout batch instances" phase (NEXT_SESSION.md) can draw on directly - not built here, out of this task's scope, but recorded so that phase does not have to rediscover the source.

activityType corrected from "aggregate" to "test" (2026-09-28, Dan's own instruction, GB5) - diggs:PlannedActivityTypeEnumType's own documentation defines "aggregate" as "will create a sample or samples by aggregating EXISTING SAMPLES" (sampleScope should then cite more than one sourceSampleRef), which does not describe this design: a grout mix is produced by blending raw constituents (cement, SCM, aggregate, water), not by combining existing samples. "test" - "will produce a test, standard or blank sample that does not relate to any field sample or sampling feature" - is the value that actually matches, the identical correction just applied to the realized side (diggs:SamplingActivity[sa-gb-1]'s own activityType).

DesignGroutMix.placementDescription: CMC rigid inclusion columns across the treated area; the Load Transfer Platform is a separate compacted granular fill (DesignRILTP) and does not use this concrete mix. Very Severe exposure per 70-TMSS-03 Table 8B, Mg<1000 ppm row: Type I cement, Silica Fume admixture.

DesignRILTP.gml:name: LTP design — Building Raft and TR Tunnels

Remark.content: This zone's own CMC design row (FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Table 4) combines the Building Raft foundation with the Transformer (TR) cable tunnels; Figure 2 of the same report labels only "BUILDING RAFT FOUNDATION" and does not delineate the tunnels separately. supportedStructureType states the structure that governs this platform's design, per PB1's convention, rather than attempting to state both.

ltpThickness matches this zone's own LoadTransferPlatform/impliedLTPThickness (elevationTopLTP minus the working platform elevation, built at GUS1) - both ultimately read off the same Bottom of Foundation and CMC Cut-off Level values in FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00's own project levels. youngsModulus, unitWeight, cohesion, frictionAngle and poissonsRatio are the LTP fill design parameters FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 states identically in Tables 1, 2 and 3 - one shared platform-material specification, not zone-varying - duplicating what the same five values are cited as on the site model's own GeoUnitObservation[unitName="LTP"] per group (GUS1); stated explicitly here too since a design object should not depend on a ground model existing to carry them.

ltpThickness matches this zone's own LoadTransferPlatform/impliedLTPThickness. This zone's own elevationTopLTP is not independently sourced - it is the "background" elevation of Group 3's stepped site-model composite (docs/build/GUS1/NOTES.md), shared with zone-bw because neither is singled out for its own elevated structure, not a value stated anywhere specifically for "Remaining Area." youngsModulus, unitWeight, cohesion, frictionAngle and poissonsRatio are the LTP fill design parameters FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 states identically in Tables 1, 2 and 3 - one shared platform-material specification, not zone-varying - duplicating what the same five values are cited as on the site model's own GeoUnitObservation[unitName="LTP"] per group (GUS1); stated explicitly here too since a design object should not depend on a ground model existing to carry them. A platform can have a stated thickness and material without a single named supported structure, which is exactly this zone's case.

supportedStructureType is an inferred, unconfirmed judgment call: this zone's CMC length (12 m, FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Table 4) is shorter than the heavy power-equipment zones (Power Transformer, Shunt Reactor, Auxiliary Tr, all 14-18.5 m), suggesting lighter equipment - breaker stands, disconnect switches, instrument transformers - more typically founded on discrete isolated footings than a heavy equipment block. Neither the foundation type nor the equipment itself is named in the project record; flagged for review rather than treated as settled.

DesignMeasurement.gml:name: PLT-201 plate load test design - shunt reactor foundations

Remark.content: Contractor response (Rev.02) to ASEC comment 8 on submittal DTS-114 (FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 PDF p.27): one plate load test for the main building raft foundation, one for the power transformer foundations, one for the shunt reactor foundations and one for the remaining outdoor foundations, exact locations as per the ASEC site consultant; drawing FSTSA31047-DWG-ABD-9001 legend (PDF p.18): PLATE LOAD TEST - 4 NOS. This design is the shunt reactor foundations (realized on CMC-942, zone-sr) test. Planned maximum stress 225 kPa: method statement FSTSA-EN31313-MS-CMC s.10.1 item 8 loads to a maximum of one and a half times the design bearing pressure, and FTR s.6.1 gives that pressure as 150 kN/m2. 150 kPa is the platform design pressure (DesignRITreatedArea risd-01); the test applies it to a column head. Read as conservative for the column, which carries only part of the platform load (Dan, 2026-10-04). The platform settlement limits (LTPS-RAFT, LTPS-FOOTING) are not a limit on this test and no performance criterion is stated for it. The plate diameter is the method statement's (s.10, 620 mm); the certificates of the realized tests state other diameters. The method statement places the plate on the exposed column head on a sand bed (s.10.1 items 2-3), where the Rev.02 response says the test is on top of the load transfer layer; the realized tests follow the method statement. samplingFeatureDesignRef cites the design of the column the test was made on, as assigned by the location table on the drawing; the plan itself fixes only the group.

PlateLoadTest.beddingMaterial: sand bed, 25 mm maximum thickness (method statement FSTSA-EN31313-MS-CMC s.10.1)

DesignMeasurement.gml:name: ZLT-201 zone load test design - building raft platform

Remark.content: Owner comment 8 on submittal DTS-114 (FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 PDF pp.27-28) asked for a zone load test for the main building raft foundation, with acceptance criteria; none was stated. The only statement of the test's intent is the test report (CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx sheet 5, ELCM EL/20481JO/29415/24): design bearing pressure 150 kN/m2, maximum test pressure 225 kN/m2 (150 percent of design). No zone load test method statement is in hand. The platform design pressure is risd-01's designLoad (150 kPa); here the tested element is the platform, so testLoadPercentDesignLoad applies as stated. The platform design cited is riltpd-brt; the report does not say which building zone the test lies in, and its four columns (CMC-155, 156, 172, 173) all lie in zone-brt. Plate size is not planned: the report states 2.0 m x 2.0 m, which belongs to the realized test.

DesignMeasurement.gml:name: Pile integrity test design - CMC production layout test locations

Remark.content: The plan is the CMC production layout drawing EN31313-DWG-SD-6001 Rev 0 as annotated in the integrity test report (ATIS, 3 February 2025; FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 4, PDF p.121): 55 original test pile locations, 41 marked as used and 14 marked as not used. The 14 not used carry the reasons the drawing states: head surface not leveled (CMC-417, 476); head surface not exposed, under backfilling (CMC-902, 316, 318, 323, 325, 327, 563); crane location (CMC-53); backfilled area for ZLT (CMC-155, 200); backfill stockpile (CMC-500); not reached 7th day age (CMC-576). CMC-646 and CMC-1058 are marked as used but have no reflectogram in the report; they are taken as planned and not tested, marked as used in error (Dan, 2026-10-05). The nodes of measurementLocation are the reference points of the 55 planned columns, indexed 0 to 54 in ascending column number. Five tests were made on 28 November 2024 at locations marked as identified test locations, which are not part of the plan; of the planned locations, eleven were replaced on 21 December 2024 by new locations (and five dropped); see the realized tests.

An earlier testing layout, EN31313-DWG-SD-8001 Rev 0 (05-09-24, issued for approval; FTR PDF pp.48 and 101), lists 10 integrity test locations PIT-201-01 to 10 (CMC-819, 962, 317, 62, 399, 37, 279, 997, 1036, 1082). It is read as superseded by the 55 location layout and is not the plan; only CMC-819, 399 and 317 were tested.

The report cites no test standard. The method is a low-strain pulse echo test, the method of ASTM D5882 and of NF P94-160-2; neither is cited here as the method. Report s.2.0 and s.3.0 (FTR PDF pp.118-119): pile heads cut to sound concrete level, leveled, cleaned and smoothed by grinder; test made with a PIT Collector device, a one pound hand-held hammer with an integral cushion and an accelerometer fixed with wax; three hammer blows averaged at each test location; wave speed taken as 4000 m/s. Owner comment 8 on submittal DTS-114 asked for integrity tests for confirmation of verticality and soundness of the drilled CMCs, with a detailed method statement and acceptance criteria (FTR PDF pp.27-28); the method statement the contractor attached is not in the project record. No percentage of columns to be tested is stated.

Equipment.gml:name: Hand-held hammer, one pound, with integral cushion
Accelerometer fixed to the pile head with wax, PIT Collector

Remark.content: Thin by design, per GroutSpecificationType's own documentation - carries no fields of its own here; the strength requirements are stated as sibling PerformanceCriterion objects attached through partOfSpecificationRef (GB5, 2026-09-28). Cited from DGM-MIX-A's own programSpecificationRef - the one mix design covering the whole program (see that design's own remarks).

Owner minimum compressive strength for construction, 30 MPa: ASEC review of submittal DTS-114 R03, ref. 40611302/46438-J/24, 13/11/2024, comment 7 (construction 30 MPa, design 25 MPa; the contractor responded that for construction 30 MPa will be considered), in the scanned appendix of FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 (PDF pp.61-67). The final report and CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx sheet "7. Concrete Compressive" (A10/D10) still label the pass/fail threshold with the 25 MPa design value; the owner's higher construction value governs acceptance and is applied to all 41 field batches (all 41 satisfy it; 28-day range 40.7-54.5 MPa). A structural, not durability, minimum - contrast crit-grout-strength-durability-min below, which is higher and separately authorized.

70-TMSS-03 Rev.02 Table 8B, Note 1 (appended to GSL-31136-Geotech-Final-Report.pdf; clean structured extraction in GSL-31136-Geotech-Report-MA .xlsx sheet "7. Chemical Analysis" row 30) - the durability-governing minimum for Very Severe/Severe exposure, independent of which admixture row applies. Matches DGM-MIX-A's own strengthDesign, which keeps this as the higher, governing value over crit-grout-strength-qc-min's 25 MPa.

Same authority and limit as crit-grout-strength-qc-min (30 MPa, the owner construction minimum; CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx sheet "7. Concrete Compressive" A70/B70 still shows the 25 MPa design value), stated at the mean statistic rather than the per-batch minimum - mirroring the mean/minimum pair GroutSpecificationType's own strengthAverage/strengthMinimum fields carried before GB4 retired them in favour of sibling PerformanceCriterion objects. The 41 real batches actually achieved 46.58 MPa average (28-day, sheet7 B67) against this requirement, comfortably clearing it - the achieved value is evidence, not restated here as the limit; it belongs on the realized GroutBatch/measurement objects the still-open "realized grout batch instances" phase (NEXT_SESSION.md) will build.

70-TMSS-03 Rev.02 Table 8B (appended to GSL-31136-Geotech-Final-Report.pdf; clean structured extraction in GSL-31136-Geotech-Report-MA .xlsx sheet "7. Chemical Analysis" row 21/F column, "Max Cl in Concrete %") - a fixed 0.10% ceiling across every exposure row regardless of admixture route. The table extract states neither which chloride fraction nor what basis; the limit is read as the WATER-SOLUBLE chloride content, as a mass fraction of the cement (reading of the 70-TMSS-03 text supplied 2026-09-30). Acid-soluble chloride (designProperty.xml#acid_soluble_chloride_content_in_concrete) is a distinct quantity; the extract states no acid-soluble limit, so none is modelled. Modelled as a DesignConformanceCriterion, not a PerformanceCriterion (GB5/GB6): a mix-composition requirement, not an emergent behaviour of the cured material. Compliance is shown by testing (constituent materials and hardened concrete, for example ASTM C1218/C1218M), and no such test is presented for this project, so the criterion is not evaluated - see ev-grout-mix-a. The property is the water-soluble chloride content in concrete - distinct from properties.xml#chloride_content (soil/groundwater, the exposure condition that selects the Table 8B row) - direction-neutral; the "maximum" is carried by operator/limit below.

70-TMSS-03 Rev.02 Table 8B, Very Severe (Mg<1000)/Silica Fume row - "Min. BM Content (Kg/m3)" = 390, the same row DGM-MIX-A's own design uses directly as its binder content. A mix-proportioning requirement verified from the batch record, not a tested physical property - see designProperty.xml#binding_material_content. The property is binding material content, direction-neutral; the "minimum" is carried by operator/limit below, not the property's own name (corrected, GB7, 2026-09-28, Dan's observation - the entry was originally minted as minimum_binding_material_content, inconsistent with every other entry in this dictionary and in properties.xml, none of which bakes a comparison direction into its name).

70-TMSS-03 Rev.02 Table 8B, Very Severe (Mg<1000)/Silica Fume row - "Max W/BM" = 0.40, the same row DGM-MIX-A's own design uses directly as its water/binding-material ratio (distinct from waterCementRatio=0.4348, which excludes the SCM replacement from the denominator). A mix-proportioning requirement verified from the batch record, not a tested physical property - see designProperty.xml#water_binding_material_ratio. The property is water/binding-material ratio, direction-neutral; the "maximum" is carried by operator/limit below (corrected, GB7, 2026-09-28, Dan's observation).

FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 work method statement, p.54: "Slump test shall not be lower than 180mm and not greater than 260mm", performed before placement. The method statement does not make clear whether that is once per batch or for every CMC; the criterion is stated per placement and the subject kind of a check (batch or column) would follow whichever applies. Not evaluated: the report presents no slump records. DGM-MIX-A's former slumpDesign of 120 mm was removed - it had no source in the project reports (carried over from an earlier draft) and lies outside this range; the design states no slump target of its own, the acceptance range lives here.

FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 work method statement, p.54: compressive strength testing at a minimum of 1 sampling per 100 m3 of concrete placed. Stated as a rate (0.01 per m3). Not evaluated: Appendix 5 reports one averaged strength per age per casting date and does not say how many samplings stand behind it, so the count cannot be shown. Were the samplings recorded, each would be its own sample with its specimens and tests citing it, and one check per batch (that batch the only subject, its 28-day tests the evidence) would compare the count of distinct samplings to the batch volume.

Fortis Soil Technologies work method statement FSTSA-EN31313-MS-CMC Rev 00 (05/09/2024), reproduced in FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 2, s.9.3, p.9 of 27 (FTR PDF pp.44, 54): "Discharge of concrete, shall be completed within 3 hours after the introduction of mixing water to cement & aggregate" (the same section gives a concrete expiry time of 180 minutes). Not evaluated: only the date of casting is recorded for each batch (FTR Appendix 5), not the batching or placement times.

FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 s.7.1.1 and s.8 (Table 4 note): the Load Transfer Platform is "good quality well compacted granular material"; no geosynthetic reinforcement or cementitious binder is mentioned, hence platformType unreinforced_granular_fill. LTP works were executed by the Main Contractor, not Fortis. Applies to all nine LTP zones; the two building zones additionally cite a settlement specification that is based on this one. No fill gradation envelope is stated in the FTR or the geotechnical report, so aggregateGradationCurveCoarseLimit/FineLimit and materialType are not populated. Thin by design: the requirements are sibling criteria attached through partOfSpecificationRef.

Specializes LTPS-GEN for the building raft zone. Allowable settlement 50 mm for raft foundations: ASEC (EDD) review comments on submittal DTS-114 R03, ref. 40611302/46438-J/24 dated 13/11/2024, comment 7 (the owner asked that the contractor change the allowable settlement values to 50 mm for raft and 25 mm for isolated foundations; the contractor responded that this was complied with in the revised report), reproduced in FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 s.4 and s.6.2, and consistent with GSL-GT-31136 Table 12 (raft settlement at most 50 mm).

Specializes LTPS-GEN for the building isolated-footing zone. Allowable settlement 25 mm for isolated foundations - same sources as LTPS-RAFT (owner comment 7; FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 s.4; GSL-GT-31136 Table 12, isolated settlement at most 25 mm).

FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 s.8 (note under Table 4): "The compaction requirements for this LTP are EY > 65 MPa"; also CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx sheet 1 (Min. LTP Young modulus (Ey) > 65 MPa) and LTP_Parameters_Jazera.xlsx s.2. The source states a strict inequality, carried as gt. The report names no test method for demonstrating it: the contractor submittal response (Rev.02) proposed plate load tests on top of the LTP, but no such test is reported. The owner review comment asked that compaction be stated as a modified AASHTO density needed to obtain the required Young modulus; the contractor noted it, and the report states only the modulus, so no density criterion is modelled. The design value is 60 MPa (DesignRILTP/youngsModulus); this acceptance limit is separate. Not evaluated: there is no LTP modulus evidence.

Allowable settlement of the foundation on the finished LTP over the CMC network (the composite of platform, columns and ground), at the 150 kPa design pressure - not a property of the platform fill alone. Source and limit: see LTPS-RAFT. Evidence is the zone load test (ZLT-201, 2.0 m x 2.0 m, BS 1377 Part 9 s.4.1, CMC 155/156/172/173, 3.36 mm at 150 kPa), which was performed on the compacted ground after the platform was built, on the four columns of zone-brt. The compared value is the settlement at the criterion's 150 kPa on the loading leg of m-ZLT-201, interpolated from the loading increments by the settlement definition's value_at binding. Evaluated in ev-zone-load-test.

Allowable settlement of the foundation on the finished LTP over the CMC network, at the 150 kPa design pressure; limit 25 mm for isolated foundations. See crit-ltp-settlement-raft for what the limit applies to and for the evidence available. Not evaluated.

One specification for the whole program: nothing in the project record varies by zone except the design length, which is stated on the column designs. Technique: Controlled Modulus Columns formed with a 600 mm closed (lost-cap) displacement auger that pushes soil sideways and removes no spoil (FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 s.7.1.1-7.1.2), hence columnType drilled_displacement_column and riInstallationMethod full_displacement. Column material is governed by GS-MIX-A. The limits are the sibling criteria that cite this specification through partOfSpecificationRef: crit-col-position, crit-col-length-min, crit-col-length-deviation, crit-col-refusal, crit-col-embedment, crit-col-verticality, and the composites crit-col-depth-or-refusal and crit-col-acceptance.

Method content that states no limit and so is not a criterion: setting out is by the execution drawings from the main axis set out by the general contractor; for each column the operator checks that the machine mast is vertical and well positioned to the setting out (Fortis Soil Technologies work method statement FSTSA-EN31313-MS-CMC Rev 00 (05/09/2024), reproduced in FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 2, s.9.1, p.9 of 27); depth is controlled by driving to the depth on the approved layouts, the operator recognising the bearing layer by rising hydraulic pressure and falling penetration speed (s.9.2).

The requirements on HOW each column is installed, as distinct from RICS-GEN, which states what the finished column must be. Sources: Fortis Soil Technologies work method statement FSTSA-EN31313-MS-CMC Rev 00 (05/09/2024), reproduced in FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 2 (s.9.1 setting out, s.9.2 depth control) and FTR s.7.1.2 (method of execution): a 600 mm displacement auger closed at its base by a lost cap, driven to the required depth or to refusal, then extracted without unscrewing while the cement mixture is fed through the stem. The refusal criterion (crit-col-refusal) is part of this specification; the method statement's other content states no limit.

Recording parameters: FTR s.7.1.2 step 2a says the drilling parameters are observed in the cabin on a monitor ("drilling speed, depth, torque applied, etc.") and step 2d that the speed of extraction is controlled by the operator from the Machine Monitor. Depth, penetration rate, torque and pull speed are therefore stated as required; the report does not say they are stored, and no drilling record from this project is in hand.

Fortis Soil Technologies work method statement FSTSA-EN31313-MS-CMC Rev 00 (05/09/2024), reproduced in FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 2, s.9.1, p.9 of 27 (FTR PDF pp.44, 54): "the tolerance is 200 mm in each direction". ASSUMPTION (Dan, 2026-10-03): read as a radial distance in plan, 0.20 m, which is what the dictionary entry position states; the per-axis reading is available through the easting_position_deviation and northing_position_deviation entries.

Not evaluated. The deviation needs the designed setting-out coordinates, and the setting-out drawing the inspection requests cite (EN31313-DWG-SD-6001) is not in the project record. The as-built coordinates alone cannot give a deviation, and the offsets of the as-built columns from the idealized layout grids are an artefact of how those grids were fitted (median 0.37 m), not setting-out error.

Owner minimum length 10 m: ASEC review of submittal DTS-114 R03, ref. 40611302/46438-J/24, 13/11/2024 (FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 PDF pp.21-28), comment 7 ("minimum length of CMC shall be 10 m"); the contractor adopted it ("the revised report consider the Minimum length of CMC 10.0 m"). An absolute as-built length, distinct from crit-col-length-deviation, which compares length with the design length. A hard requirement: it is a member of crit-col-acceptance.

Length against design: as-built column length minus the design length of the DesignRIColumn the column cites (FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Table 4, p.16, by zone). ASSUMPTION (Dan, 2026-10-03): the sources state no permitted shortfall, so a column should be no shorter than designed (limit 0 m). Driving may stop short of the design depth only at refusal (FTR s.7.1.2 step 2c, "when the required depth is reached or refusal criteria"), so this is one member of crit-col-depth-or-refusal. A failed check here is not by itself a non-conformance; it becomes one only if refusal cannot be shown for that column.

FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 s.7.1.2 step 2c (p.12) and the Table 4 note: "refusal criteria (5cm penetration for 2 consecutive minutes)". ASSUMPTION (Dan, 2026-10-03): read as less than 5 cm of total penetration in 2 minutes, not 5 cm per minute; the interval is stated by the interval_duration evidence condition.

Evaluated only for the six columns that have an installation record (CMC-430, CMC-1097, CMC-942, CMC-666, CMC-80, CMC-1043); each check's subject is the column's construction activity (constructionActivityRef), whose installation record it reads, and compares the depth the tool gained in the two minutes of downward push that end when it first reaches its maximum depth - the pause at total depth is not part of the window - with the limit. All six records are SYNTHETIC: no drilling records exist for this project, and the four rig logs at the repo root are from a different job (FSTSA 25053, Jubail, 2026). Every other column has no record and is not evaluated.

CompositeAcceptanceCriterion.gml:name: Column driven to design depth OR to refusal

Remark.content: FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 s.7.1.2 step 2c: "when the required depth is reached or refusal criteria (...) the driving is stopped". The column is acceptable if it reached its design length or stopped at refusal. Satisfied where the length member is satisfied; otherwise it depends on the refusal member, which can be evaluated only where an installation record exists (CMC-430 stopped at refusal and is satisfied; CMC-1097 was still advancing and is not satisfied) and is undetermined elsewhere. The refusal member's subject is the column's construction activity, not the column; its verdict applies to the column through the activity's samplingFeatureRef.

ASEC review of submittal DTS-114 R03, ref. 40611302/46438-J/24, 13/11/2024 (FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 PDF pp.21-28), comment 6: the minimum depth of the columns "shall be sufficient enough to cross the Sabkha layers and any lose clayey layers"; the contractor replied that all columns are "fully embedded into the bearing layer, well clear of the sabkha zones". ASSUMPTION (Dan, 2026-10-03): the bearing layer is the shallowest layer of the site model with a Young's modulus of at least 20000 kPa and no softer layer below it. That is the Silty sand layer (guo-g1-siltysand, top -3.23 m RL) in the Transformers model, the Silty sand to sandy silt layer (guo-g2-siltysandtosandysilt, top -7.86 m RL) in the Buildings model, and the Clean sand to silty sand layer (guo-g3-cleansand, top +2.34 m RL) in the Default Site model. Embedment is the elevation of the layer top minus the column toe elevation; the limit 0 m means the toe is at or below the top of the layer.

Each check cites the bearing layer as its evidenceObservationRef. A column is assigned to a site model by its plan position against the model footprints (Transformers first, then Buildings, otherwise Default Site), which agrees with its load transfer platform zone for all 1099 columns. The "loose clayey layers" of the comment are not separately modelled.

No numeric limit appears in the project record: Fortis Soil Technologies work method statement FSTSA-EN31313-MS-CMC Rev 00 (05/09/2024), reproduced in FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 2, s.9.1, p.9 of 27 says only that the operator checks the machine mast is vertical; the owner asked for integrity testing "for confirmation of verticality and soundness" with acceptance criteria (ASEC review of submittal DTS-114 R03, ref. 40611302/46438-J/24, 13/11/2024 (FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 PDF pp.21-28), comment 8), and the verticality row of CMC_Parameters_Jazera.xlsx is blank. ASSUMPTION (Dan, 2026-10-03): 2 %, horizontal deviation divided by depth, times 100.
Checks are by declaration. The pile integrity tests (ASTM D5882 low-strain) detect cracks and section changes and do not measure inclination, and no inclination was recorded.

CompositeAcceptanceCriterion.gml:name: Column acceptance: minimum length AND embedment AND design depth or refusal

Remark.content: The three requirements a column must meet together (Dan, 2026-10-03): the 10 m owner minimum length is a hard requirement; the column must not stop short of the top of the bearing layer; and it must have reached its design depth or refusal. Position and verticality are separate criteria and are not part of this combination.

MeasurementSpecification.gml:name: Plate load test specification - rigid inclusion column heads

Remark.content: Requirements on how the column-head plate load tests are carried out, from the Fortis Soil Technologies work method statement FSTSA-EN31313-MS-CMC Rev 00 (05/09/2024) s.10, reproduced in FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 2 (PDF pp.44-47). The method statement itself is cited through measurementMethod (spec-ms-cmc). The requirements the schema can check on the realized test are carried by the criteria that cite this specification through partOfSpecificationRef. The method statement's increments, hold and stabilization are criteria that cite this specification (crit-plt-increments-min, crit-plt-hold-min, crit-plt-stabilization); its plate, bed and dial gauges are planned values on the planned procedures of dm-PLT-201 to 204 and are not criteria. No criterion on the settlement the test produces exists in any source: FTR s.6.2 lists the measured settlements under a heading of allowable settlements and states no limit, and method statement s.10.2 asks only that the allowable bearing pressure and settlement be evaluated. The platform settlement limits (LTPS-RAFT, LTPS-FOOTING) apply to the platform, not to a column.

MeasurementSpecification.gml:name: Zone load test specification - load transfer platform

Remark.content: Requirements on how the zone load test on the load transfer platform is carried out. No zone load test method statement is in hand; the test report (CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx sheet 5) cites BS 1377 Part 9 s.4.1 and states the loading it applied. The requirement the schema can check on the realized test is carried by crit-zlt-max-stress. The settlement the test must not exceed is the platform settlement limit of crit-ltp-settlement-raft (LTPS-RAFT); this specification states no limit of its own.

Method statement FSTSA-EN31313-MS-CMC s.10.1 item 8 (FTR PDF p.46): load "to a maximum of one and a half times design bearing pressure"; design bearing pressure 150 kN/m2 (FTR s.6.1), so 225 kPa. Read as a minimum the test must reach: a test taken above it still conforms (PLT-204 went to about 294 kPa and is flagged on its record). Compared with the maxTestStress of each plate load test's procedure, converted to kPa. The two certificates that state their loading in kgf/cm2 (PLT-201, 2.25 kgf/cm2 = 220.6 kPa; PLT-204, 3.00 kgf/cm2 = 294.2 kPa) are compared after conversion, so PLT-201's recorded 2.25 kgf/cm2 falls 4.4 kPa short of 225 kPa. Evaluated in ev-load-tests.

The zone load test is taken to at least 150 percent of the design bearing pressure: 225 kPa, from the test report's stated maximum test pressure of 225 kN/m2 = 150 percent of the 150 kN/m2 design bearing pressure (CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx sheet 5; Dan, 2026-10-04: the report's 150 percent is accepted as the source, no zone load test method statement being in hand). Compared with the maxTestStress of the zone load test's procedure. Evaluated in ev-zone-load-test against m-ZLT-201: 225 kPa reached.

Fortis Soil Technologies work method statement FSTSA-EN31313-MS-CMC Rev 00 (05/09/2024) s.10.1 items 8 and 9, reproduced in FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 2 (FTR PDF p.46): "Load shall then be applied in at least three increments to a maximum of one and a half times design bearing pressure." Counts the loading increments recorded in the test's procedure; unloading increments are not counted. Evaluated in ev-load-tests.

Fortis Soil Technologies work method statement FSTSA-EN31313-MS-CMC Rev 00 (05/09/2024) s.10.1 items 8 and 9, reproduced in FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 2 (FTR PDF p.46): "Each load increment shall be held for a minimum of 15 minutes, and until the rate of settlement rate is less than 0.02mm per 5-minute interval." This criterion is the 15 minutes (900 s), taken from the first to the last reading of each loading increment; the shortest hold over the loading increments is compared. The stabilization half is crit-plt-stabilization. Evaluated in ev-load-tests.

Fortis Soil Technologies work method statement FSTSA-EN31313-MS-CMC Rev 00 (05/09/2024) s.10.1 items 8 and 9, reproduced in FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 2 (FTR PDF p.46): each increment is held "until the rate of settlement rate is less than 0.02mm per 5-minute interval". Read as: at the end of each loading increment the settlement gained over the last five minutes is below 0.02 mm, and the largest of them over the loading increments is compared. The readings of an increment are three minutes apart, so the settlement five minutes before the last reading is interpolated between readings. This tests the recorded readings; the stabilizationCriterion recorded on each increment (0.004 mm/min = 0.02 mm per 5 minutes) restates the limit and is not the evidence. Evaluated in ev-load-tests.

MeasurementSpecification.gml:name: Pile integrity test specification - rigid inclusion columns

Remark.content: Requirements on the low-strain integrity tests of the CMC columns. The project record states no acceptance criterion for them: owner comment 8 on submittal DTS-114 asked for acceptance criteria (FTR PDF pp.27-28) and the report states only that a deviation of the plot from the straight line of a sound pile indicates a change in cross-section or cracks (FTR PDF p.119). The criteria that cite this specification through partOfSpecificationRef are therefore of two kinds: requirements on how the test is carried out, taken from the plan and the report (crit-pit-count, crit-pit-location, crit-pit-impacts-min, and crit-pit-age-or-strength with its members crit-pit-age-min and crit-pit-strength-at-test), and limits on what the records show, inferred (crit-pit-toe-depth, crit-pit-flaw, crit-pit-defect, and the composite crit-pit-acceptance). A low-strain test locates major defects and gives no information on load capacity, and its classification is not by itself grounds to accept or reject a column. The 55 tests are evaluated in ev-pit.

The plan is 55 test locations (dm-PIT). Compared with the number of integrity tests made, the realized measurements of the program with a low_strain_integrity_test kind: 55 were made, 39 at planned locations, 11 at locations that replaced planned ones and 5 at locations that were not in the plan.

Each test is made at a planned location: the horizontal distance between the column tested and the planned node the test realizes (realizesGridIndex, in the grid of dm-PIT) is within the position tolerance of the columns, 0.20 m, the limit of crit-col-position (Dan, 2026-10-05). A test with no planned node is outside the limit. A test outside the limit is not rejected: the relocations were made for access or age (see the reasons recorded at the planned locations in dm-PIT) and are accepted as is.

ASTM D5882-07 s.6.1: the average of the records of at least three impacts, and s.6.4: the number of impacts of an averaged record is recorded. Report s.3.0 (FTR PDF p.119): three hammer blows are made at each test location and the average recorded. Three is also the smallest number of similar impacts the Piletest PET User Manual allows for an easily tested pile. Compared with the averagedImpactCount of each test's procedure; the 'Avg' of each reflectogram header states it (15 to 19).

ASTM D5882-07 s.6.2: for cast-in-place concrete piles the test is made no sooner than 7 days after casting or after the concrete reaches at least 75 percent of its design strength, whichever occurs earlier; the Hong Kong Code of Practice for Foundations 2017 s.8.7 and the PDI sample specification also give 7 days. Age is taken from the end of the column's whenConstructed interval to the date tested. CMC-295 was cast on 2024-12-16 and tested on 2024-12-21, at 5 days; CMC-584 and CMC-551 at 7 days. The tester skipped CMC-576 (cast 2024-12-14, 7 days old on 21 December) as not having reached its 7th day (FTR PDF p.121). A member of crit-pit-age-or-strength.

ASTM D5882-07 s.6.2: 75 percent of design strength. Design strength is 38 MPa, the strengthDesign of DGM-MIX-A (Dan, 2026-10-05): the strength the mix was specified to reach, set by durability in the corrosive conditions, taken in place of the 25 MPa structural value; 75 percent is 28.5 MPa. Compared with the compressive strength of the cylinders of the column's batch (groutRef) tested no later than the date the column was tested. The batches' cylinders were tested at 7 and 28 days, so a column tested before its batch's 7-day cylinders has no strength result at its test age; the strength at test is then not known and the criterion is not shown to be met. For CMC-295 (batch 41, 7-day cylinders tested 2024-12-23, 33.7 MPa) the strength at the test is not known; a strength-gain curve through the 7- and 28-day results puts it near 28 MPa, about 113 percent of 25 MPa, which is context only. A member of crit-pit-age-or-strength.

CompositeAcceptanceCriterion.gml:name: Test made on mature concrete: at least 7 days old OR at least 75 percent of design strength

Remark.content: The condition on when a low strain integrity test may be made (ASTM D5882-07 s.6.2): the age or the strength is enough, whichever is reached first. A column younger than 7 days whose strength at the test is not known does not satisfy it. That is a non-conformance of the test conditions, not evidence of a defect in the column, and is accepted as is where the record is otherwise good.

ASSUMPTION (Dan, 2026-10-05): the toe depth read from a record is the depth of its deepest reflection, found working up from the bottom of the record at its first amplitude maximum (which separates the toe from internal defects, which lie above it), not the length marker the software places, and is acceptable within 10 percent of the length of the column. The assumed wave speed of 4000 m/s is uncertain by about 10 percent for concrete from one week of age (Piletest PET User Manual), and length from low-strain records by 5 to 10 percent (Webster, Rausche and Webster, 2011); a larger difference means a short column, a column that reached refusal short of design, or a wrong wave speed. Without sign; compared with the length the tester entered into the equipment for the column (the referenceLength of the test's procedure), taken as the as-built length of the column (Dan, 2026-10-06): the record holds no other length for the columns tested - the columnLength of the RIColumn is the design depth of the production workbook, not a measured length.

ASSUMPTION (Dan, 2026-10-05): a reflection above the toe of the same sign as the impact (a reduction in impedance: a neck, a crack or poor concrete; PDI, Interpretation of Results from a Pile Integrity Tester) whose height is more than 0.11 of the impact peak indicates a flaw to be reviewed. 0.11 is the reflection coefficient of an impedance ratio of 0.8, the limit between slightly damaged and damaged in the beta method (Rausche and Goble, 1979, as given by Likins and Rausche). A flaw is a cause for review, not for rejection. Applies to a record whose amplification balances the toe reflection against the impact (the practice for setting it, Piletest PET User Manual; PDI, Interpretation of Results from a Pile Integrity Tester): the relative height is then read as an approximation of the reflection coefficient (Z1 - Z2)/(Z1 + Z2) of the impedance change. A record that is not balanced, or shows no clear toe, is inconclusive for this criterion and is not failed by it. Balanced is taken as a toe reflection between 0.5 and 2 times the impact peak (the criterion's evidenceCondition on relative_toe_amplitude; the band is an assumption, Dan 2026-10-06): a check on a record outside it, or without a clear toe, is inconclusive, and a reflection above the limit on such a record is not counted as a flaw or a defect.

ASSUMPTION (Dan, 2026-10-05): a reflection above the toe of the same sign as the impact whose height is more than 0.25 of the impact peak indicates a defect. 0.25 is the reflection coefficient of an impedance ratio of 0.6, the limit between damaged and broken in the beta method (Rausche and Goble, 1979, as given by Likins and Rausche). Applies to a record whose amplification balances the toe reflection against the impact (the practice for setting it, Piletest PET User Manual; PDI, Interpretation of Results from a Pile Integrity Tester): the relative height is then read as an approximation of the reflection coefficient (Z1 - Z2)/(Z1 + Z2) of the impedance change. A record that is not balanced, or shows no clear toe, is inconclusive for this criterion and is not failed by it. Balanced is taken as a toe reflection between 0.5 and 2 times the impact peak (the criterion's evidenceCondition on relative_toe_amplitude; the band is an assumption, Dan 2026-10-06): a check on a record outside it, or without a clear toe, is inconclusive, and a reflection above the limit on such a record is not counted as a flaw or a defect.

CompositeAcceptanceCriterion.gml:name: Pile integrity: toe depth within tolerance AND no defect indicated

Remark.content: The two limits on what a record shows that indicate a column to be reviewed or replaced: the toe depth agrees with the as-built length, and no reflection above the toe reaches the defect limit. crit-pit-flaw is not a member: a flaw calls for review of the record, not for a failed acceptance. The conditions of the test (count, location, impacts, age or strength) are separate design-conformance criteria: a record made before the concrete had matured is inconclusive, not a sign of a defect. A check of this composite is satisfied where both members are satisfied, not satisfied where either is not satisfied, waived where a member is waived (accepted as is) and none is not satisfied, and inconclusive otherwise.

RIProgramBasis.gml:description: The site-wide basis the Controlled Modulus Column program design was prepared from: the standards it was prepared under, the class of calculation used, the safety format those standards imply, and the ground aggressivity adopted as its durability premise. ONE BASIS FOR THE WHOLE PROGRAM, not one per zone - FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 8 states a single method, a single in-house calculation tool and a single set of governing standards applied uniformly across all nine zones, and what varies per zone is the resulting design output, not the premise. Sources are FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 (the CMC final technical report) and GSL-GT-31136 (the geotechnical investigation it was prepared from).
RIProgramBasis.gml:name: CMC program design basis

Remark.content: CMC Final Technical Report FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC Rev.0, 17 March 2025.
CMC Final Technical Report FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC Rev.0, 17 March 2025.
CMC Final Technical Report FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC Rev.0, 17 March 2025.

Seven governing standards, which is not simply FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 2.2's list. Excluded from that list deliberately: reference [6], "ASTM. American Society for Testing and Materials", names no standard number or year and cannot be resolved to a specification; references [8] FORTIS Quality Assurance and Quality Control System & Procedures, [9] OHSAS 18001:2007 and [10] ISO 14001:2004 are contractor management-system and quality-procedure documents governing how the work is executed rather than premises the design was prepared from, so they are out of scope for a program basis (PB4) - they are candidates for the construction-activity side instead. Added beyond that list, because the design demonstrably rests on them although 2.2 omits them: NF P94-261 and NF P94-262 carry the bearing-capacity and skin-friction formulae of 8.2, and SBC 301-CR-18 is the cited source of every seismic parameter in GSL-31136 3.2 Table 1.

safetyFormat is INFERRED and is not stated by the project. FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 names no safety format anywhere, and a keyword sweep of both reports returns no "partial factor", "global factor" or any stated factor of safety value (PB4 6.5). The inference rests on 8.2's capacity chain being taken from NF P94-262 (toe bearing q_b, limit skin friction q_s, negative skin friction Ktan-delta) and NF P94-261 (q_net), which are France's Eurocode 7 national application standards and which implement Design Approach 2 - verified 2026-09-23 against CEREMA's own methodological guide to NF P94-262 rather than assumed. Weighed against it: the method actually executed is a pressuremeter/CPT correlation chain using Frank and Zhao (1982) mobilization factors, not a visible partial-factor verification, so DA2 is implied by the standards adopted rather than exercised in the calculation. Recorded as inferred per the convention PB2 established for every inferred value on this program.

Two exposureClassification values, on the two independent axes the property is repeatable for - chemical attack on the concrete and grout, and electrical corrosivity to embedded steel - not one finding stated twice. Both come from GSL-31136 and neither appears in the CMC report at all. sec_tmss_very_severe is from 5.4.3's chemical analysis (BS 1377 part 3: sulphates 5810-8515 ppm, chlorides 0.510-0.705 %, magnesium 571-954 ppm, pH 7.90-8.20), with 7.11 naming 70-TMSS-03 Rev. 02 Table 8B as the authority that sets cement type from it. palmer_very_severe is from 5.2's soil resistivity, where all six ERT stations returned 0.11-0.23 ohm-m against Table 5's 0-10 ohm-m VERY SEVERE band (Palmer 1974).

Fields left absent, checked against the full source set at PB4 rather than assumed: designWorkingLife and consequenceClass (no service life or reliability/consequence class stated anywhere in either report); designMethod and archingModel (both concern LTP load-transfer mechanics, which neither report addresses - the design is a column bearing-capacity calculation); factor (the coefficients 8.2 does state - the rheological factor alpha-M, the penetrometer bearing factor Kc, and the Frank and Zhao mobilization factors Kq and KT - are adopted correlation coefficients, not the partial or global safety factor set a safetyFormat applies, which is what diggs:DesignFactor and this type's factor element are defined for); peakGroundAcceleration (GSL-31136 3.2 Table 1 gives Ss, S1, Fa and Fv but no a_g, and deriving one from them is not code-sanctioned - ASCE 7 and SBC 301 derive site-adjusted PGA from a separately mapped PGA and its own F_PGA coefficient, neither of which the report provides).

References [2] and [3] of FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 2.1 ("CMC Design report document reference – FSTSA-EN31313-TP" and the General Plot Plan drawing WA 775920 sheet 003 rev. 00) are acknowledged but NOT built as associatedFile: diggs:AssociatedFileType/fileURL is mandatory and neither document is held or retrievable, so no real URL exists to cite and none is fabricated. [1], the geotechnical investigation GSL-GT-31136, is not an associatedFile either but for a different reason - it is already the diggs:Project this program's projectRef targets.

Per-value clauses, all from GSL-31136 3.2 Table 1 and all cited there to SBC 301-CR-18: Ss from Figure 22-1, S1 from Figure 22-2, the site class from Table 20-1 (against SPT N less than 15), Fa from Table 11-1 and Fv from Table 11-2. The report's own prose at 3.2 says "SBC 301-2008" while every row of its table cites SBC 301-CR-18; the 2018 edition is taken as correct because it is what the table rows themselves name.

peakGroundAcceleration is deliberately ABSENT. No a_g is stated anywhere in the project record, and it cannot be derived from the values here: in ASCE 7 and the codes derived from it a site-adjusted peak ground acceleration comes from a separately mapped PGA and its own F_PGA coefficient, whereas Fa and Fv apply only to the spectral ordinates. Synthesising one from Fa and Ss would apply the wrong coefficient to the wrong hazard parameter and present the result as sourced.

seismicSiteClass here is the AS-INVESTIGATED class - the ground as found, read against SPT N less than 15 in the seven boreholes of a pre-construction investigation. It is therefore neither diggs:DesignRITreatedAreaType/seismicSiteClass (the class a design predicts after improvement) nor diggs:RITreatedAreaType/seismicSiteClass (the class achieved). Both of those are left empty on this project, because nothing in the record measures or predicts a post-improvement class.

DesignBasisParameter.gml:description: Frank and Zhao (1982) toe mobilization factor Kq for coarse-grained soils, which FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 8.2 states is the value governing at this site.

Frank and Zhao (1982) toe mobilization factor Kq for fine-grained soils. Stated by FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 8.2 alongside the coarse-grained value; recorded because the report states it, although the site is governed by the coarse-grained case.
Frank and Zhao (1982) skin friction mobilization factor KT for coarse-grained soils, per FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 8.2.
Frank and Zhao (1982) skin friction mobilization factor KT for fine-grained soils, per FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 8.2.

Penetrometer bearing factor Kc used for the net bearing pressure beneath the foundation. FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 8.2 states the value adopted and notes it varies with formation level; 0.1 is the value the report writes out.
DesignBasisParameter.functionExpression: qnet = Kc x qc, with qc the equivalent cone tip resistance 1.5B below the foundation

DesignBasisParameter.gml:description: Penetrometer bearing factor Kc for the limit end bearing pressure at the inclusion toe. Read from the source standard's chart as a function of soil class and effective anchorage depth, so no single value applies and none is stated.
DesignBasisParameter.functionExpression: qb = Kc x qc, with qc the equivalent cone tip resistance below the CMC toe; Kc from NF P94-262 Figure 7 by soil class and effective anchorage

DesignBasisParameter.gml:description: The pressuremeter rheological factor alphaM, needed because the design method is pressuremeter-theory based while the soil stiffnesses were derived from CPT. Published as a table by soil type, so no single value is stated.
DesignBasisParameter.functionExpression: Em = alphaM x EY, with EY the Young's modulus of the layer and alphaM read by soil type

DesignBasisParameter.gml:description: The limit unit skin friction adopted per layer, read from NF P94-262's published curve against CPT tip resistance. A curve with no closed form, so the value elements are left absent and the figure is cited instead.
Foundation embedment depth De. FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 8.2 states it as conservatively assumed to be zero rather than measured or derived - one of the two explicit assumptions the report makes.

The average water table level adopted for design, as an elevation, per FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 4.1. Distinct from the measured groundwater: the same clause records water encountered throughout all borings at 0.65 to 0.75 m below natural ground level, and this single value is the design premise chosen to represent them.
The average existing ground level adopted for design, as an elevation, per FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 4.1, which attributes it to Fortis's own pre-treatment CPTs.

The premise, stated at FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 8.2 alongside the toe bearing formulation, that the CMCs are embedded into a competent bearing or anchorage layer. Carried as text because it is a condition asserted of the ground rather than a quantity.

Remark.content: This basis exists because the ground model is the one premise on this program that is NOT site-wide. FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 derives three soil profiles (Table 1 here), each from a different set of pre-treatment CPTs (CPT-09, CPT-10 and CPT-11), each governing a different set of LTP zones. Everything else the design rests on - the governing standards, the analysis approach, the safety format, the adopted coefficients, the exposure classification and the seismic hazard - is common to the whole program and is stated once on the master basis this one specialises through basedOnRef. Resolution is per property, most specific first, so a design citing this basis inherits all of that and adds only the ground model that applies to it.

Which zones this ground model governs is read from the citing side - the DesignRILTP objects whose own basisRef names this basis (riltpd-pt), each in turn named by its zone's LoadTransferPlatform/programDesignRef - and is not declared here. An earlier form of this object carried scope/appliesToFeatureRef pointing at those zones; removed at TAD2 as redundant with that chain, and as a reference to features this basis precedes. The grouping is the one recorded at GUS1 from Dan's explicit list, NOT inferred from the CPT groupings, and the two are not the same mapping: CPT-08 is averaged into Group 3's profile while the Building isolated footing zone it was drilled in belongs to Group 2. Neither grouping can be derived from the other.

Remark.content: No as-batched component or total-volume record exists for this batch: FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 5 (S.No. 1 of the cylinder test schedule; cast 2024-10-14, 9 CMCs, 7-day 37.5 N/mm2, 28-day 47.2 N/mm2, PASS) and its extracted copy (CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx sheet7) record only CMC-ID membership, casting/testing dates and cylinder strengths - never a batch recipe or produced volume, confirmed absent project-wide (2026-09-29 side task). This batch was therefore synthesized: totalBatchVolume is the sum of the theoretical grout volumes (design depth x diameter x 1.15 overconsumption factor, 'CMC production coordination summary.xlsx' sheet1/THEORETICAL VOLUME) of the 9 RIColumns this batch cast, rounded up to the nearest 0.5 m3 (38.9988 m3 summed); the component composition is derived from DesignGroutMix[DGM-MIX-A]'s own specified materials and limits (Type I C3A 8-14% cement, 390 kg/m3 minimum binder content, 2% assumed air content), scaled to that volume.

SCM dosage (9.2% of binder mass by weight) and W/BM ratio (0.362) are varied slightly batch-to-batch within DGM-MIX-A's own stated range (ACI 234R's 5-10% typical silica-fume dosage; W/BM at or below the design's 0.40 ceiling) to avoid presenting 41 batches as mechanically identical; binder content is held at the design's own 390 kg/m3 minimum throughout.

This batch was therefore synthesized: totalBatchVolume is the sum of the theoretical grout volumes (design depth x diameter x 1.15 overconsumption factor, 'CMC production coordination summary.xlsx' sheet1/THEORETICAL VOLUME) of the 23 RIColumns this batch cast, rounded up to the nearest 0.5 m3 (81.2475 m3 summed); the component composition is derived from DesignGroutMix[DGM-MIX-A]'s own specified materials and limits (Type I C3A 8-14% cement, 390 kg/m3 minimum binder content, 2% assumed air content), scaled to that volume.

SCM dosage (8.1% of binder mass by weight) and W/BM ratio (0.377) are varied slightly batch-to-batch within DGM-MIX-A's own stated range (ACI 234R's 5-10% typical silica-fume dosage; W/BM at or below the design's 0.40 ceiling) to avoid presenting 41 batches as mechanically identical; binder content is held at the design's own 390 kg/m3 minimum throughout.

DELIBERATE NONCONFORMANCE, Dan's instruction (2026-09-29): this batch uses Fly Ash in place of DGM-MIX-A's specified Silica Fume SCM (Table 8B's Mg<1000 ppm/Very Severe row names Silica Fume specifically for this exposure), and its water/binding-material ratio is set to 0.480, above crit-grout-wbm-max's 0.40 ceiling - a synthetic non-conforming batch for exercising conformance verification against DesignConformanceCriterion[crit-grout-wbm-max]. LithologySystem.gml:description: Interpretive soil column of lithology classifications based on direct observations of discontinuous SPT samples. Consecutive samples sharing a classification are consolidated into one layer, each layer extending to the top of the next, so the column is continuous over the full depth of the borehole.

Remark.content: Analytical results reported on page 57 of the GSL geotechnical final report (GSL-GT-31136, "ANALYTICAL RESULTS", tested 20-Jun-24, completed 23-Jun-24, ambient temperature 22 degC). The report cites BS 1377 Part 3 but does not state whether the sulfate, chloride and magnesium determinations are water-soluble or acid-soluble, so the generic propertyClass entries are used here rather than the basis-specific ones (sulfate_water_soluble, sulfate_acid_soluble, etc.), which exist for sources that do say.

MaterialTest.gml:name: MIX-A Grout Batch 1 - 7-day cylinder compressive strength

Remark.content: Result from FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 5 (S.No. 1, "7-Day Strength"): the average strength of the batch's cylinders at 7 days, reported to one decimal; individual cylinder values and the number of cylinders tested are not reported. Test method ASTM C39 is attributed by inference (cylinder compressive test on an ASTM-referencing report); the appendix names no standard and says nothing about how the specimens were made, cured or prepared.

measurementTechnique.formula: arithmetic mean of the batch's cylinder strengths at 7 days, as reported in Appendix 5

Zone load test ZLT-201 on load transfer platform zone-brt, over CMC-155, 156, 172 and 173, 22 December 2024. ELCM (Eastern Laboratory for Construction Materials) job EL/20481JO/29415/24, form GFT-424, "Full Scale Load Test (BS-1377 P-9)", test no. ZLT 1 (S/Station Building), project Al Jazeera Palace S/Station, client Fortis, 2.0 m x 2.0 m plate, weather fair, signed Imran Qadri. Readings are from the handwritten field sheets, FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 PDF pp.80-84; the calibration certificates are PDF pp.85-99. The test was inspected and accepted by ASEC-PDC (West) on RFI C-63 (FTR PDF p.61) on 22-Dec-24. Location: the footprint is the square through the four column positions (CMC-155, 172, 173, 156; 2.00 m sides, 4.0 m2), which are the columns the plate was placed over, at the top elevation of the load transfer platform (6.85 m, zone-brt elevationTopLTP); the plate edges themselves were not surveyed. Stresses are recorded as printed (38, 75, 113, 150, 188, 225 kPa, in a column headed "Applied Load (Kg)"); the nominal 25 % increments of the 150 kPa design pressure are 37.5, 75, 112.5, 150, 187.5 and 225 kPa, which are 150, 300, 450, 600, 750 and 900 kN on 4.0 m2 (appliedLoad). The pressure column, headed Kg/cm2, holds the jack pressure in bar (0, 53, 105, 157, 210, 262, 314 bar). Stages: 15 stages as in the report's Table 1 (FTR) - a zero reading at 10:10 and a 15 min wait; a seating (pre-loading) cycle, 38 kPa for 15 min then released to 0 for 15 min, headed PRE-LOADING on the sheet; then loading 38, 75, 113, 150, 188, 225 kPa, and unloading 188, 150, 113, 75, 38, 0 kPa. Hold times differ from Table 1: 38, 75 and 113 kPa were held 60 min, 150 and 188 kPa 90 min (the 60-min settlement-rate remark exceeded 0.25: "0.29 > 0.25" at 150 kPa, "0.46 > 0.25" at 188 kPa, and 0.03 and 0.11 at 90 min), 225 kPa 120 min; unloading stages 30 min. Rate remarks printed on the sheet, units not printed: 0.07 (38 kPa, 60 min), 0.04 (75), 0.17 (113), 0.02 (225, 120 min). The 0.25 limit is the only criterion on the sheet and its unit is not printed, so no stabilizationCriterion is recorded. Reading times 0, 1.5, 3, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60 (90, 120) min. Series: one series per stage, each reading with jack pressure, the four dial gauges and their mean in mm (printed in 0.01 mm), the settlement printed, and the air temperature. The outcome is the last reading of each stage. Settlement is the mean dial reading / 100 truncated to 3 decimals. The temperature is blank at 10:10. Transcription: every row's gauge readings were checked against the printed mean. Gauge cells that were illegible or disagreed with the printed mean were set to the nearest digits that reproduce the printed mean: 10:25 gauge 3 = 39; 12:59 gauge 4 = 172; 13:04 gauge 4 = 161; 14:01 gauge 1 = 256; 15:34 gauge 4 = 473; 15:41 gauge 2 = 575; 16:01 gauges 3, 4 = 400, 500; 18:04 gauge 2 = 774; 19:04 gauge 3 = 539; 19:05 gauge 1 = 460; 19:35 to 19:38 gauge 2 = 759; 21:05 and 21:06 gauge 3 = 494; 21:35 gauge 3 = 426 (second stage at 21:35); 21:40 gauge 3 = 415; 10:41 gauge 1 and 2 read 21 and 36. Where a settlement was hard to read the value computed from the mean is used: 21:35 (end of the 38 kPa unloading) is 5.465 mm from the mean 546.50, while the report's Table 1 prints 5.415 mm; and the first reading of the final unloading, 21:35, is 4.685 mm. The 150 kPa unloading stage jack pressure is 210 bar (confirmed). Settlement at the stage ends otherwise equals Table 1. Equipment: four STARRETT 25-4081 dial gauges GCDG-109 to 112 (the report's table prints GCGD), a WIKA Bourdon-tube pressure gauge P.G.212739-47-9, and two POWER TEAM 80225 hydraulic jacks HJGC-05 and HJGC-06; the sheets do not say which jack or whether both were used. Each carries its RCLS calibration certificate (pp.86-99). The report conclusion (Table 3): settlement 3.36 mm at 150 kPa, 6.29 mm at 225 kPa, residual 4.51 mm; no shear failure; "PASS - well below 50 mm allowable".

Remark.content: Pile integrity test of CMC-819 on 28 November 2024: Piletest PET reflectogram, the scanned page FTR PDF p.123, p.123 row 1 (header C 4000 m/s, Amp 10, F 0, planned length 10.0 m, Avg 15). It is not one of the planned locations of dm-PIT. The values are the heights of the plotted trace above its flat level before the impact, divided by the height of the impact peak (the highest point at the impact line of the plot); the trace is on a scanned page, digitized from a 300 dpi render as the centre of its line at every second pixel column (about 0.035 m). Depths are those of the plot's depth axis, from 0 m to the end of the record, which can run past the end of the column. The samples before 0 m are not carried. Toe: the deepest reflection of the record, found working up from the bottom, at its first amplitude maximum, 11.47 m (0.16 of the impact peak); the same maximum is found with the significance limit at 5, 10, 15 and 20 percent of the largest positive reflection.

SYNTHETIC installation record. No Jazeera drilling record exists. The record is shaped on the four BAUER OmniBox logs from the FSTSA 25053 Jubail job (depth against time, torque pressure, up and down speed) and extended with the full property suite a rig logs; values are generated from the project site model (Default, g3) Young's modulus and unit weight, with random variation, at 1 s intervals, and are not measured data. Boundary wall column driven 1 m short of its 16 m design length and stopped at refusal: the last two minutes of push gain 0.030 m (under the 0.05 m limit).

One continuous stream: push to total depth, a pause at total depth, then withdrawal with grout. Cells that do not exist in a phase (for example grout pressure during drilling, penetration rate during withdrawal) carry the property null value -9999. Grout volume is cumulative; the final volume is 5.499 m3 against a theoretical 4.877 m3 that already includes the 1.15 overconsumption factor, higher where the column crosses the sabkha. The rig and the cutting tool are ASSUMED to suit the generated record: a displacement auger of 600 mm outer diameter (FTR s.7.1.2), and a rotary drive rated to bound the generated torque pressure (297 bar), torque (240 kN.m) and rotation (30 rpm).

Remark.content: Evaluation of the six acceptance criteria attached to GS-MIX-A (the grout specification of DGM-MIX-A) against the 41 realized GroutBatch objects. FIVE criteria are evaluated: crit-grout-wbm-max and crit-grout-binder-content-min per batch from the value the batch itself records (determination measured); crit-grout-strength-qc-min and crit-grout-strength-durability-min per batch from that batch's 28-day strength test (statisticScope evidence: the source reports one averaged result per batch and age, so the minimum over a batch's evidence is that result; Appendix 5 itself passes or fails each batch); crit-grout-strength-qc-mean once over all 41 batches' 28-day tests (statisticScope population; derived - the mean of the 41 cited results, Appendix 5's 'Average 28-Day Strength').

crit-grout-chloride-max (water-soluble chloride content) is deliberately NOT evaluated. Acceptance against it requires testing - of the constituent materials and of the hardened concrete - and no such test is presented for this project, so there is no value to compare; a design mix does not by its nature put chloride content within a limit, and a declared verdict would assert what nothing supports. The criterion remains in GS-MIX-A. Likewise NOT evaluated: crit-grout-slump (the report presents no slump records) and crit-grout-sampling-frequency (the number of samplings behind each reported strength is not stated).

Synthetic data: every GroutBatch here was synthesized (see each batch's own remark) - the W/BM ratios, and the binding material content (390.0 kg/m3 on all 41, restating the 390 kg/m3 minimum the batches were built from), are not as-batched records. The strength results are the real Appendix 5 28-day averages. Batch 3 is a deliberate nonconformance on W/BM (0.480 against a 0.40 maximum).

NonConformance.gml:name: Grout batch 3 - W/BM above maximum

Remark.content: Deliberate synthetic nonconformance. The batch also substitutes Fly Ash for the specified Silica Fume SCM; only the W/BM breach is a criterion here. The disposition is a placeholder chosen only because the element is mandatory - no decision about this batch was made.

Evaluation of the criteria attached to RICS-GEN against the 1099 realized RIColumn objects. EVALUATED: crit-col-length-min, crit-col-length-deviation and crit-col-embedment from recorded and modelled values (columnLength, the design length of the cited design, the column centerline and the bearing layer of its site model), crit-col-verticality by declaration, and the composites crit-col-depth-or-refusal and crit-col-acceptance where they can be determined. crit-col-refusal (subject: the column's construction activity) is evaluated for the six columns that have a synthetic installation record (CMC-430, 1097, 942, 666, 80, 1043). NOT EVALUATED: crit-col-position (no designed setting-out coordinates) and crit-col-refusal for every other column (no drilling records); crit-grout-discharge-time on GS-MIX-A is not evaluated either (no batching or placement times).

Outcomes: length-min 1099 satisfied (shortest column 10.0 m); embedment 1099 satisfied (smallest embedment into the bearing layer 2.89 m); length-deviation 874 satisfied and 225 not satisfied (222 boundary wall columns built 1 m short of 16 m, 3 outdoor equipment columns 2 m short of 12 m). crit-col-depth-or-refusal and crit-col-acceptance carry a check only where the design length was reached (874 columns, OR satisfied); for the 225 shorter columns the verdict depends on refusal. Two of them have an installation record: CMC-430 stopped at refusal (OR and acceptance satisfied) and CMC-1097 was still advancing (OR and acceptance not satisfied, with NonConformance nc-CMC-1097-depth). For the other 223 no check is recorded and, deliberately, no NonConformance: a shortfall against design is a member failure, not yet a failure of the requirement. The four PLT-tested columns (CMC-942, 666, 80, 1043) also carry refusal checks; they reached design depth, so refusal is not satisfied and the OR is satisfied through length.

Synthetic data: the verticality checks are declarations (the 2 percent limit is itself an assumption, see crit-col-verticality), and the embedment values are computed from the column centerline and the layer tops of the three ground models, which are themselves interpretive.

NonConformance.gml:name: CMC-1097 stopped short of design depth without refusal

Remark.content: Deliberate synthetic nonconformance. The column stopped 2 m short of its 12 m design length and its installation record shows it still advancing (0.800 m in the last two minutes of push), so refusal is disproved and neither member of the depth-or-refusal requirement holds. The disposition is a placeholder chosen only because the element is mandatory - no decision about this column was made.

AcceptanceEvaluation.gml:name: MS-PLT plate load test acceptance - four tests

Remark.content: Evaluation of the four criteria attached to MS-PLT (crit-plt-max-stress, crit-plt-increments-min, crit-plt-hold-min, crit-plt-stabilization) against the four realized plate load tests m-PLT-201 to 204, from the values recorded on each test's procedure and increment readings. Each value was computed independently of the dictionary's bindings and checked against them (docs/build/PLT3). 16 checks.

Outcomes: 15 satisfied, 1 not satisfied. PLT-201 (m-PLT-201, CMC-942) was loaded to 2.25 kgf/cm2 = 220.65 kPa against the required 225 kPa (the other three reached 225, 225 and 294.2 kPa; a test above the minimum conforms). Every loading increment of every test was held 900 s or longer (the maximum-load increment of PLT-201, 202 and 203 longer), every test applied four or more loading increments, and the settlement gained in the last five minutes of an increment was at most 0.0167 mm (PLT-202 and PLT-204) against the 0.02 mm limit. The PLT-201 shortfall is recorded as non-conformance nc-PLT-201-maxstress, disposition accept as is (Dan, 2026-10-05). The zone load test is evaluated in ev-zone-load-test.

NonConformance.gml:name: PLT-201 loaded to 220.65 kPa, below the 225 kPa minimum

Remark.content: The certificate of PLT-201 (CMC-942) states a maximum load of 2.25 kgf/cm2, which is 220.65 kPa: 4.35 kPa, 1.9 percent, below the 225 kPa (1.5 times the 150 kPa design bearing pressure) that crit-plt-max-stress requires. Disposition accept as is, recorded on Dan's instruction (2026-10-05); no source document states a decision on this test. The requirement itself is unchanged.

AcceptanceEvaluation.gml:name: MS-ZLT zone load test acceptance - ZLT-201 on zone-brt

Remark.content: Evaluation of the zone load test ZLT-201 (m-ZLT-201, CMC-155/156/172/173 on zone-brt) against crit-zlt-max-stress (MS-ZLT) and crit-ltp-settlement-raft (LTPS-RAFT), plus the owner's declared acceptance on RFI C-63. The maximum test stress is read from the test's procedure (225 kPa, 150 percent of the 150 kPa design bearing pressure; Dan, 2026-10-05). The settlement is the loading-leg settlement at the criterion's 150 kPa evidence condition, taken from the 150 kPa increment of the loading series (6 loading increments, seating cycle excluded): 3.360 mm against the 50 mm limit; the unloading leg passes 150 kPa again at 6.177 mm and is not the value. Both values were computed independently of the dictionary's bindings and checked against them (docs/build/ZLT1/checks).

AcceptanceCheck.gml:name: RFI C-63 - ASEC-PDC acceptance of the zone load test

Remark.content: Declared by the owner's representative. Request for Inspection C-63 (FSTSA31047-FTR-CMC-00 PDF p.61), dated 21-Dec-24, inspection 22-Dec-24 4:00 PM, "Zone Load Test (ZLT) on CMC# 155, 156, 172 and 173", drawing EN31313-DWG-SD-6001: ASEC-PDC (West) comment "According to the test results from the third party and allowable settlement, the test results are accepted", box APPROVED, signed 22-Dec-24. The declaration is against the allowable settlement, so it is recorded on crit-ltp-settlement-raft.

AcceptanceEvaluation.gml:name: MS-PIT low strain integrity test acceptance - 55 tests of the CMC columns

Remark.content: Evaluation of the 55 low strain integrity tests (pit-CMC-*, 28 November and 21 December 2024) against the criteria of MS-PIT: the count (crit-pit-count, one check over all tests); for each test the position (crit-pit-location), the number of averaged impacts (crit-pit-impacts-min), the age (crit-pit-age-min, with crit-pit-strength-at-test where the age is not met, and the composite crit-pit-age-or-strength), the toe depth against the length (crit-pit-toe-depth), the flaw and defect limits on the reflections above the toe (crit-pit-flaw, crit-pit-defect) and the composite crit-pit-acceptance. Values are taken from the dictionaries' value bindings (designProperty, properties) applied to each test.

Position: 39 tests are at their planned node; the 11 tests at nodes of planned columns that were replaced and the 5 tests at locations not in the plan are waived and each has a NonConformance, disposition accept as is, with the reason from the plan (Dan, 2026-10-05). Age: CMC-295 was tested at 5 days with no strength result of its batch; its age and strength checks are not satisfied, the composite is waived with a NonConformance. Toe depth: compared with the length the tester entered, taken as the as-built length (Dan, 2026-10-06); the 6 tests beyond the limit are waived and accepted as is, each with a NonConformance; where no clear toe is stated the check is inconclusive. Flaw and defect: the relative height of a reflection above the toe is read as a reflection coefficient only on a balanced record, one whose toe reflection is 0.5 to 2 times the impact peak (the evidenceCondition of the two criteria, an assumption); on any other record the check is inconclusive, and each such check states the reflection that exceeds the limit and why it is not counted as a flaw or a defect. The one defect on a balanced record (CMC-295) is waived and accepted as is with a NonConformance; the flaws (4) are causes for review and carry no disposition. Outcomes: toe depth 3 inconclusive, 46 satisfied, 6 waived; flaw 46 inconclusive, 4 not satisfied, 5 satisfied; defect 46 inconclusive, 8 satisfied, 1 waived; acceptance 42 inconclusive, 6 satisfied, 7 waived. The composite crit-pit-acceptance is not satisfied if a member is not satisfied, waived if a member is waived, satisfied if both are satisfied, otherwise inconclusive.

The tests are the realized measurements that cite dm-PIT (the subjects listed): 55 against the 55 planned locations. Not every planned location was tested - 5 were dropped and 11 were replaced - but the count of tests made is the plan's.
